adaptive_revision_disclosure.reason_for_revision: R1 required the candidate to pass the same fixed allclose tolerance against both bitsandbytes fused eager and a BF16-dequantized explicit FP32 linear reference. The post-failure 126-case audit proved that 35 cases and 297 output elements have disjoint allowed intervals, so the conjunction is mathematically unsatisfiable.
known_r1_observations_used_to_design_r2: The existing candidate compiled and ran on sm_89, including K=2560,N=10240.
The first complete R1 correctness run stopped in k_proj_full_nonshared / wide_normal / seed 20260916 with max_abs 0.125.
All frozen-oracle interval conflicts in the 126-case audit occurred in wide_normal; 13 of 14 variants and all three R1 seeds were affected.
The existing candidate matched an independently reconstructed FP32-weight semantic reference in the focused failing-case diagnosis, but this diagnosis is not an R2 holdout result.
No formal K2 candidate performance, ncu, or reconnection measurement was started under R1.
adaptive_revision_disclosure.interpretation_rule: R2 is a transparently adapted confirmatory attempt. It must never be presented as if its oracle or holdouts had been chosen before observing R1.

single_hard_correctness_oracle.name: explicit_fp32_nf4_semantic_reference
single_hard_correctness_oracle.definition: Decode high/low nibbles and both nested scale levels explicitly in FP32 according to semantic_contract, materialize W_fp32 only inside the untimed reference path, run torch.nn.functional.linear on FP32 activation and W_fp32, then cast the output to BF16.
